clean_story:
"Machine health. Predictive care.
The term condition monitoring describes watching a machine’s vital signs, like a doctor checks a pulse. A vibration sensor on a wind turbine blade detects wobble before the metal cracks. A temperature probe in an electric motor warns of overheating before wires melt. These tools turn invisible wear into data, letting engineers act before failure stops a factory or grounds a plane. In 1970, airlines adopted vibration analysis to prevent jet engine failures, cutting delays by 30 percent. Today, wireless sensors and algorithms track pumps, conveyors, and generators, often spotting faults weeks in advance. The precision comes from thresholds: a bearing’s vibration jumps from 2 millimeters per second to 5, triggering an alert. No guesswork. Just numbers. Three related subjects are predictive maintenance, vibration analysis, and industrial sensors."
